**What it is:** MeshCFO is a Python project described as "The auditable multi-agent CFO." Three agents (Finance, Strategy, Compliance) produce board-style finance outputs: forecasts, investment cases, and board decision packets. Each claim is meant to trace to the agent, reasoning step, and source that produced it.

**What it does:**
- Runs a brief through the three agents on a shared context engine, then synthesizes a CFO artifact and audit trail.
- Wraps each session in the Consensus Hardening Protocol (CHP), which includes a deterministic review of the output and a lock progression. A named human confirmer is required for the final "LOCKED" state.
- Writes each recommendation to a signed, append-only JSONL audit ledger using HMAC-SHA256 chaining, so tampering is detectable.
- Stores state in SpacetimeDB and offers a CLI (`cfo-os`) and a Python API.

**Is it a neatHack entry?** The page doesn't say. Nothing on it mentions neatHack.

**When was it created?** The page doesn't give a creation date. It shows 30 commits and a "© 2026" site footer, but no repository creation date.

Highlights:
NEAT solves the AI coding context problem. It constructs a live deterministic model of your codebase — static code and live runtime behavior fused into one graph — and hands your AI agents the grounded, full-stack context they need to query, code, debug, and write rules against it. This achieves the following:
- Coding LLMs hallucinate less & are more accurate.
- Rather than endlessly grepping files and guessing problems, NEAT provides time-travelling error logs along the model's nodes and edges so the LLM can infer exactly what's wrong.
- Rules & Policies allow agents to write new features while adhering to rules set by previous features, other LLMs, or engineers. For example, only use postgres for services x and y, and mongoDB for services p and q (the possibilities are endless).

TL;DR The deterministic grounded truth of code for your agents. 

NEAT is in active development ... Capability ships as patch releases on the `npx neat.is` surface; see ... what's on deck.
...
the live edges populate
...
At the center of NEAT is **one live graph** of your system, fused from two streams into a single model you can query many ways:
...
Both streams land on the same nodes, so the graph holds what your code *declares* and what your system *does* side by side. From there ... the useful questions fall out of one model: what would break if this node dies (blast radius), what broke first (root cause), which architectural rules a change would violate (policies), and where declared intent and observed reality part ways (divergence). Same graph, different traversals.
...
The graph is exposed to AI agents through sixteen MCP tools. Ten read the graph — `get_root_cause`, `get_blast_radius`, `get_dependencies`, `get_observed_dependencies`, `get_incident_history`, `get_divergences`, `get_graph_diff`, `get_recent_stale_edges`, `check_policies`, `semantic_search` — and six (`neat extend`) let an agent close instrumentation gaps for libraries the bundled OTel set doesn't cover, driven by a versioned instrumentation registry.
...
Divergence reports what *is*. Policies let you assert what *should be*. A `policy.json` in your project declares ... rules as assertions over ... same graph — for example, "only `service:billing` and `service:orders` may connect to `postgres:primary`," or "no file may call `legacy-api.internal`." Because the rules run against the live graph, they evaluate against both what your code declares and what production actually does.
...
- **`neat policies`** lists what's currently violating, scoped to a node with `--node`, or dry-run a change with `--hypothetical-action`.
- **`check_policies`** hands the same answer to an AI agent over MCP, so an agent writing a new feature can see which rules it would cross and the assertions it's working within — the rules previous features, other agents, or your engineers already set.
...
## Wire NEAT into your agent

NEAT's MCP server is listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.neat-technologies/neat`, so registry-aware editors can install it in one click:
...
Each button wires the `@neat.is/mcp` server via `npx -y @neat.is/mcp` and points it at your local daemon; set `NEAT_CORE_URL` to target a non-default one. For Claude Code:
...
The `neat-mcp` binary above assumes a global install. Without one, run `neat skill --apply` instead — it writes the same `mcpServers.neat` entry using `npx -y @neat.is/mcp` so the server resolves without a global binary. Either form reads `NEAT_CORE_URL` for the daemon URL; set it to point the agent at a non-default daemon.

In any Claude Code session, ask: *"Why is checkout-svc failing?"* NEAT walks the graph and answers with a traversal path, edge provenances, a confidence score, and a recommended fix.
...
This installs two nudges so your agent queries the graph before it falls back to raw text search:

- **A Claude Code search-nudge hook** — a `PreToolUse` hook that, when the agent reaches for `Grep`/`Glob` or a Bash `grep`/`rg`/`find`, injects a note pointing it at `semantic_search`, `get_dependencies`, and `get_divergences` first. It is a gentle, non-blocking nudge: the search still runs. It merges into `~/.claude/settings.json` without touching your other hooks, and re-running is idempotent.
- **Agent-agnostic graph-first guidance** — a markdown block (`GRAPH_FIRST.md`, also written to `~/.neat/neat-graph-first.md`) to paste into `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `.cursorrules`, so agents on any harness get the same steer.

The hook is specific to Claude Code; other harnesses (Codex, Gemini, Cursor) rely on the guidance block instead. `neat hooks --print-hook`, `--print-guide`, and `--print-settings` show each piece without installing.
...
The `neat skill` and `neat hooks` commands above are the à-la-carte way to wire NEAT in. On Claude Code you can get all of it — the MCP graph tools, the graph-first search-nudge hook, and the skill — in one install, as a plugin:
...
The plugin lives in this repo under `plugin/` and is installed straight from GitHub — nothing extra to publish. It bundles exactly the same MCP server config and search-nudge hook the à-la-carte commands write, so both paths behave identically; pick whichever you prefer. ## 🔗 MCP integration

The agent gets 11 tools the moment Claude Code restarts after `neatcode claude install`:

| Tool | When the agent calls it |

**Rules + validation**

| Tool | When the agent calls it |
| --- | --- |
| `get_rules` | Returns active rules, candidates, rejected list, and repo context for curation flows. |
| `validate_diff` | Pre-flight on a planned change. Returns violations + four-option suggestions block. |
| `propose_rule_from_prompt` | Inspects a user utterance for rule-language ("never", "must", "always"). Surfaces a structured proposal. |
| `accept_proposed_rule` | Promote a single proposed rule into `skills.yaml`. |

All deterministic. No LLM call inside the server. The agent is the brain; neatcode is the spine.
...
## 📐 How rules emerge
...
1. **Heuristic mining** — `neatcode skills derive` proposes candidates above the coverage threshold. Four primitives mined today: `decorator-required`, `annotation-forbidden`, `naming-pattern`, `folder-naming-convention`.
2. **Prompts** — when the user says *"all classes with @Controller must use @UseGuards"*, the agent calls `propose_rule_from_prompt`. A local keyword classifier — **no LLM in the loop** — extracts a structured candidate. User confirms, agent runs `skills accept`.
3. **Manual** — hand-edit `.neatcode/skills.yaml` (create it on first rule). The schema is documented and stable.

Rules are validated **bidirectionally**:
- A diff that violates a rule → four-option UX (record exception · time-bounded · supersede the rule · abort).
- A rule that no longer matches the codebase → can be superseded with an entry in `decisions.yaml`.
...
## 🏗️ Architecture
...
Every relationship gets a confidence label (`EXTRACTED` | `INFERRED` | `AMBIGUOUS`); the validator **never fires on rules built solely from `AMBIGUOUS` edges**. The repo-root-relative `qualified_name` is the FK that ties nodes, edges, rules, and decisions together. There's no LLM in the hot path of any MCP tool — the LLM lives in the agent harness (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex), and neatcode is the spine.
...

# An agent that fixes your servers, repairs configs and asks before anything risky (MHacks 26) 

This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge
...
Nightshift is an agent that has terminal access to your machines while their owner is away. It finds the problem and proposes the fix. A gate decides whether the fix may run, and a small board on the desk is where a human says yes.

A service dies. Within a few seconds the agent has read the logs, checked a library of known fixes and written a log. If the fix is safe, it runs alone. If it needs a person, the FREE-WILi board turns orange and shows APPROVE. A green press lets that one command run, exactly once. The device snapshots itself first, checks its health afterwards, and rolls back by itself if the check fails.

The model never decides what it may do. A policy file does, so a confused or manipulated model can't talk its way up a level. Ask it to delete files and the request hits a rule; nothing runs.

Devices dial out to the database, so none of them opens an inbound port. Fixes earn trust one at a time: after three verified successes a fix stops asking and the board says EARNED. One failure sends it back to asking.

Approvals are live rows, so the board, a phone page and the dashboard change together. The phone can approve over mobile data through a private Tailscale link. And two hard shakes of the board revoke everything the agent was allowed to do.
...
The demo is a test bench. Faults are injected on demand into containers that play servers, and into a Pixel 9 Pro over adb, so every run starts from a known failure and plays the whole loop.
...
FREE-WILi. The board is the input and the status light. Its screen fits one short word, so each state gets one: IDLE, APPROVE, FIXING, HEALTHY, EARNED, BLOCKED. Seven LEDs add color, so a glance across the room says what the agent is doing. Five buttons approve, deny, undo and show events, and the accelerometer drives the double-shake kill switch. A small Python bridge passes events along as JSON lines and reconnects by itself when the board re-enumerates.

Gemini API. The agent loop calls Gemini with function calling and says why before it acts. A fix costs about 3,000 to 6,000 tokens, roughly a tenth of a cent. If the network drops, the loop switches to a local Qwen model on the laptop GPU.

SpacetimeDB. Approvals are rows with rules attached: who may approve, who may revoke, when a grant expires. The database enforces them and pushes every change to whatever is subscribed, so a board, a phone and a browser behave as one surface.

The page doesn't mention neatHack. It has no offer, signup, or credit details for it, so I can't tell you anything about it from this content.

The page does describe some general access and output:

- **Signup:** The site offers a "Launch Month" banner with "Your first model, free," plus "Try it free now" and "Talk to a Human" buttons. It doesn't say what the free trial includes or whether it uses credits.
- **Pricing:** A Pricing link exists, but the page doesn't include plan details.
- **Model output:** The example shows a 2027 growth plan with a hiring scenario. It includes ending ARR, Q4 operating income, ending cash, and a payback period, along with upside, base, and downside cases. The operating forecast is quarterly and covers ARR, revenue, gross profit and margin, account executives, quota capacity, payroll, operating expenses, operating income, and ending cash.

**Ari** is cfo.ai's product: an AI assistant that acts as a "personal CFO." It builds financial models from your actuals and shows how decisions would change them.

- **Product:** You ask a question, and Ari builds or updates the model. The page's example asks whether the company can afford to hire two account executives, and Ari models that scenario.
- **Outputs:** Financial models and scenarios, P&L and cash flow views, headcount, board summaries, and first drafts of board decks. It also sends proactive updates, such as flagging a margin issue or a churn increase. It can build one-off tools, like a custom revenue dashboard.
- **Integrations:** Ledger (NetSuite, QuickBooks), payroll/HR (Rippling, ADP), banking (Mercury, Brex), billing (Stripe, Paddle), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot), warehouse/BI (Snowflake, Looker), and spreadsheets (Google Sheets, Excel). The page describes integrations as read-only.
- **Access:** Web app, plus MCP access from your own terminal.
- **Infrastructure:** The page describes REAM, a spreadsheet system the company built for agents rather than humans.
- **Pricing:** The page offers a free first model and a free trial, but it doesn't list plans. The pricing page is linked separately.
- **Founders and parent company:** The page doesn't mention founders or any parent company. I can't confirm whether Runway is connected.
- **Is it an "AI CFO"?** The page calls Ari a "personal CFO" and uses "AI" in its domain, but it doesn't use the phrase "AI CFO." It's a fair description of an AI tool that performs CFO-style financial modeling and analysis, though it isn't a replacement for a licensed finance professional.

# Agent Orchestrator architecture

Agent Orchestrator is a long-running Go daemon that supervises multiple
parallel AI coding-agent sessions. Project sessions own isolated Git
worktrees. Projectless standalone workers own AO-managed plain-directory
workspaces. Every session uses one interface mode at a time.

A TUI session runs its agent inside a native PTY/ConPTY runtime, with tmux as a
legacy or fallback runtime. A Chat session runs a native protocol controller
without an agent terminal runtime. Codex and all ACP Chat processes run in
detached per-session hosts, so replacing the daemon or desktop app does not
stop an in-flight turn. The ACP host also preserves connection setup, JSON-RPC
correlation, pending interactions, and acknowledged prompt replay while the
replacement daemon rebuilds its typed controller.

A durable handoff can move a compatible native conversation between TUI and
Chat, but both controllers are never live at once. The daemon coordinates both
modes through the same session, lifecycle, workspace, storage, and observation
boundaries.

### Session interface handoff

An interface switch is a controller replacement inside the existing AO session,
not a new session. The session id, optional project, workspace, lifecycle facts,
and provider-native conversation id stay the same. For project sessions, branch
and PR ownership also stay the same. Only the mode-owned controller changes.

The generic coordinator lives in `session_manager`; providers opt in through the
small `AgentInterfaceHandoff` capability only after their TUI resume id and Chat
protocol id are proven to name the same native conversation. Claude Code and
Codex currently satisfy that contract. Merely having a Chat/ACP driver is not
enough to enable switching for another harness.

The native ID handed over is the current Terminal conversation, which can differ
from the last Chat provider (for example after replacing an orchestrator). This
does not prove that the new provider inherited the old context. Session Manager
reserves a `ChatProviderHandoff` only from a matching durable TUI→Chat transition;
ordinary resumes retain the exact-handle check. Chat resumes the verified target,
reconciles only its provider scope, and prepares a visible context boundary.
Lifecycle and SQLite atomically publish that boundary, native history, controller
generation, and any project-narrative ownership transfer, checking the observed
owner, head, sequence, and controller fence again after provider I/O. Prior rows
remain intact, but are not represented as context inherited by
...

(loopback + LAN)
...
The mobile app is a second thin renderer over those same session resources. It
branches on the session's persisted `mode`: TUI attaches the existing mux PTY,
while Chat reads the paged conversation projection and uses the durable CDC SSE
stream only for targeted invalidation/reconnect. Sends, approvals, input,
provider configuration, compaction, rollback, and shell creation remain daemon
commands; no provider or lifecycle policy is implemented in React Native.
...
## Terminal multiplexing

The mux is the primary agent controller only for TUI-mode sessions. Chat-mode
sessions have no agent runtime handle and never attach their provider through
tmux. They may still open session-scoped shell terminals as a worktree escape
hatch; those shells are separate resources and do not become the agent
controller.
...
## Browser runtime bridge

Browser automation uses ... dedicated local socket (`browser.sock` on Unix,
`ao-browser[-dev]` named pipe on Windows) between the daemon and Electron. The
daemon owns command authorization/correlation; Electron owns the actual browser
targets. Commands never use the supervisor liveness socket and never enable an
unauthenticated remote-debugging port.

Accept UPI, Indian-issued cards, and Apple Pay in INR from customers in India. Understand RBI subscription mandates, the 48-hour delay, and mandate limits.

Accept UPI, Indian-issued cards (Visa, Mastercard, and RuPay), and Apple Pay from customers in India. UPI carries more than 80% of India’s digital payment transactions by volume. Dodo Payments supports subscriptions on UPI and Indian-issued cards through RBI-compliant mandates.
...
Unlike most alternative payment methods, UPI and Indian-issued cards, including Visa, Mastercard, and RuPay, support recurring payments through RBI mandates.
...
| Method | Type | Subscriptions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UPI | QR code | Yes* |
| RuPay Credit | Card | Yes* |
| RuPay Debit | Card | Yes* |
| Apple Pay | Digital wallet | Yes* |

*Subscriptions require RBI-compliant mandates with special processing rules. The 48-hour processing delay applies to recurring charges on all Indian-issued cards, UPI, and Apple Pay. A payment billed in INR must be at least ₹5.00 and at least the equivalent of the USD minimum: $0.50 for one-time payments and $1.00 for subscriptions. See Minimum Amounts.

API Method Types

Pass these values in `allowed_payment_method_types`:

| Type | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `upi_intent` | UPI via QR code |
| `credit` | Credit cards, including RuPay |
| `debit` | Debit cards, including RuPay |
| `apple_pay` | Apple Pay, on Apple devices. See Apple Pay in India |

Checkout offers UPI only as `upi_intent`. If `allowed_payment_method_types` lists `upi_collect` but not `upi_intent`, UPI doesn’t appear at checkout.
...
```
// `client` is an initialized DodoPayments client.
const session = await client.checkoutSessions.create({
  product_cart: [{ product_id: 'pdt_123', quantity: 1 }],
  allowed_payment_method_types: [
    'upi_intent',
    'credit',
    'debit',
    'apple_pay'
  ],
  billing_currency: 'INR',
  customer: {
    email: '[REDACTED_EMAIL]',
    name: 'Priya Sharma',
    phone_number: '+919876543210'
  },
  billing_address: {
    country: 'IN',
    zipcode: '560001'
  },
  return_url: 'https://example.com/success'
});
...
UPI appears at checkout only when all of these are true:

1. The billing country is India (`IN`).
2. The billing currency is INR.
3. For subscriptions from merchants outside India, Adaptive Currency is enabled. One-time checkouts don’t need it if the product is priced in INR.

If you’re a merchant outside India and Adaptive Currency is disabled, your customers can’t pay for subscriptions with UPI.
...
Subscriptions paid with UPI or Indian-issued cards run on RBI (Reserve Bank of India) mandates, which add rules that other payment methods don’t have.
...
Set the mandate floor for INR e-mandates with the `mandate_min_amount_inr_paise` field, in INR paise (₹1 = 100 paise).

This setting only affects e-mandates registered for Indian-issued cards (Visa, Mastercard, RuPay) on INR subscriptions. UPI subscriptions follow their own AutoPay flow and aren’t affected.
...
| Level | Where to set | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per request | `mandate_min_amount_inr_paise` on a checkout session or subscription | One transaction |
| Merchant | Business-level default, if one is configured | All your INR subscriptions |
| System | — | ₹15,000 default |

Dodo Payments uses the first value that’s set: the per-request override, then the merchant setting, then the system default. To set the floor, pass `mandate_min_amount_inr_paise` in the request body when you create a checkout session. The deprecated Create Subscription endpoint accepts the same field.

A higher floor lets you make larger one-off charges later, such as plan upgrades or usage-based overages, without asking customers to authorize again. A lower floor keeps the customer’s authorization closer to the actual billing amount, but leaves less room for future variable charges.

It recommends treating agent runs like a data pipeline, with structured traces, auto-tagging, continuous evals on production runs, and human feedback that feeds AI evaluators. content.content:
**Entire** is a developer platform for Git hosting and agent session tracking. It describes itself as "Fast, distributed, independent Git hosting for agents and humans."

**Products covered on the page:**
- **Checkpoints:** A checkpoint is created for every commit, pairing the code change with the agent session that produced it.
- **Sessions:** Conversations are captured and linked to git history automatically. Secrets are detected and redacted before storage.
- **CLI:** Installed with one command in a repo. It's open source under the MIT license and works with agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor.
- **Git hosting:** Regional mirrors of your GitHub repos, with data centers in US East, EU Central, and Australia, plus India and the US listed as in-region options.

**Not covered:** The page doesn't mention Trails, entire-graph, or the founders, so I can't describe them.

**Hackathon use:** The page doesn't mention hackathons. Based on its features, participants could use the CLI to automatically record their agent sessions, search past work for the reasoning behind code, resume work with a different agent, or have several agents review a branch in parallel. This is my inference, not something the page states.

Crustdata is a data provider built for AI agents. It covers company and people data, live headcount, and job postings, and it delivers that data through APIs and webhooks.

**What it does**
- Crustdata describes itself as a San Francisco company that supplies real-time company and people data through clean APIs and webhooks built for AI agents. It was founded in 2024 and part of Y Combinator's Fall 2024 batch.
- Its sources include LinkedIn, the SEC, funding announcements and milestones, employee ratings, product reviews, web traffic, among others.

**Headcount and job postings**
- Its company data covers company headcount, headcount by function, job openings, web traffic, social follower counts, funding rounds & details, with historical data for each.
- Job listings are available as structured data: one source says Crustdata can retrieve structured job listings with 30+ data points and 35 search filters.
- A Jobs API is part of the suite, and one source says the company's bulk datasets include real-time headcount, people change, funding, website traffic, and product review data at scale.

**People data**
- The Person Enrichment API can be queried by LinkedIn URL or email. One vendor page says it returns 90+ datapoints including job title, company, tenure, and contact details.
- People search lets you filter by title, location, seniority, function, and recent job changes.

**Real-time monitoring (Watcher)**
- The Watcher API sends push notifications. Its events include company grows or declines in headcount, company lists a job posting for a certain title or technology, person changes jobs, and funding rounds.
- Notifications are delivered by webhook. One vendor says they arrive within hours of occurrence.

**AI agent access**
- Crustdata has a Web Search API for agents, and a community-built MCP server connects it to tools like Claude Desktop and Cursor (a community-built server (lord-Rheagar/crustdata-MCP)). That server is third-party, not an official Crustdata product.

**Caveats**
- Much of what I found comes from third-party listing and integration sites, not Crustdata's own documentation. Check Crustdata's official docs for exact endpoints, field counts, and refresh rates.
- Pricing is unclear. One directory says specific pricing tiers and credit system details are not explicitly provided.
- The "real-time" claim is not uniform. The same directory notes that the exact refresh rate for the flat file data is monthly, so the live behavior applies to the API and webhooks rather than the bulk files.
- The sample agent output in the Improvado listing (for example, "127 companies matching criteria") looks illustrative, not measured results.

## neatHack research brief (as of Oct 11 2026)

### VERIFIED FACTS

**Rules (main site [neatlogs.com/hackathon](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon))**
- Submissions open Mon Oct 12, 7:00 PM IST. The planned close is about 11:55 PM IST, and Discord will announce the final cutoff. Winners are announced Oct 16.
- You submit by quote-posting the official neatlogs submission post on X. The quote carries your team, project name, public repo and demo link. The site's "Submit on X" button appears only once the window opens and the official post is live, so **that post does not exist yet**. neatlogs and cfo.ai will engage with the first 50 quote tweets.
- The demo video must be 3 minutes or less. For each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai it must cover architecture, implementation, runtime, reasoning and result.
- Commits must be dated inside the hackathon. Code written before Oct 10 is not allowed.
- Evidence they ask for:
  - before/after agent runs with numbers compared
  - neatlogs trace links
  - Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output
  - a cfo.ai business plan covering pricing, costs, revenue and runway
  - a run where the agent recovers from a failed action
  - #neatHack posts
- Mentors score the entries. The community winner is judged separately.
- Credits:
  - LiteLLM: $20 per team (Nova and Claude models)
  - AWS: $25, for the first 350 teams to check in. Bedrock is excluded.
  - Crustdata: 5k credits per participant
  - cfo.ai: credits via [cfo.ai/neathacks](https://cfo.ai/neathacks). A card is required, and they say to cancel the subscription right away.
- An older version of the page ([neatlogs.com/hackathon/1](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/1)) had a building-in-public sub-rubric:
  - Social content: 25
  - Reach and engagement: 15
  - Demo and storytelling: 30, framed as "problem → agent → failure → Neatlogs → solution"
  - Community contribution: 15
  - Presentation: 15
  - That version also said the community prize goes to the post with the most likes that tags @neatlogs and #neatHack, and that bought likes disqualify.
- [Luma](https://luma.com/s5blr882) adds only a few things the main site doesn't: hosts Simran Sachdeva, Ajay Yadav and Aj Yadav; about 1,359 going; teammates must each register separately under the same team name. Registration is closed.

**Kickoff (Ajay's recap, [x.com/bettersayAJ/status/2108889671321469349](https://x.com/bettersayAJ/status/2108889671321469349))**
- About 1,400 developers from 40 countries, and #neatHack trended on X.
- Talks:
  - Siqi Chen (@blader): six years of ups and downs before cfo.ai went viral
  - TheVibeFounder: "distribution is EVERYTHING"
  - Haimantika: how fast Entire has grown
  - Prateek: how he acquired the orchestrator.inc domain
- neatlogs itself launches publicly Oct 12.
- On Oct 11, Ajay quote-tweeted the **Crashtest** team's cfo.ai plan, which was built from neatlogs trace costs: about $0.117 per run, about 79% gross margin, and hiring timing versus runway. He then asked cfo.ai for a native neatlogs integration ([status/2109147787510321652](https://x.com/bettersayAJ/status/2109147787510321652)).

**Participant projects** (from the [#neatHack feed](https://nitter.cf/search?f=tweets&q=%23neatHack), replies to [neatlogs' "drop your project" post](https://x.com/neatlogs/status/2108855688026042598), and GitHub)

⚑ = finance, CFO, invoices or payments. ★ = agent-company, agent-economics or agency.
- ⚑★ **Tally** (@battarchicken): a "CFO for your agent fleet" that caps spend per task.
- ⚑★ **AgentFinOps** (@magnuskrypt): profiles agent fleets, refactors bloat, and syncs the savings to cfo.ai.
- ⚑★ **Margin** (@Jemii_aHH): packages agent work into priced, capped, verified, auditable units for outcome-based billing. **This is the closest to Syncly's "pay agents per job".**
- ★ **somora** (@somora_ai): a self-hosted AI agent team with shared memory.
- ⚑ **Munshi** (@ShivamKuma31380): an AI accountant that closes the month's books and recovers from imbalances.
- ⚑ **MarginGhost** (@K2Chaturvedi): finds supplier invoice overcharges against contracts and POs, then builds recovery cases. neatlogs quote-tweeted it.
- ⚑ **Spend Radar** (@AakarshDhi43154): compares budget and invoices against competitor hiring data from Crustdata.
- ⚑ **Vigil** (@Musa_Ais, [github.com/MusaAis/vigil](https://github.com/MusaAis/vigil)): a payment-ops agent that fixes payment failures, with an independent verifier. Runs on simulated payments.
- ⚑ **DisputePro** ([github.com/prabhat-gp/neathack-upi](https://github.com/prabhat-gp/neathack-upi)): resolves UPI payment exceptions before RBI deadlines.
- ⚑ **ProofAgent** ([github.com/kaulastudies/proofagent-neathack-2026](https://github.com/kaulastudies/proofagent-neathack-2026)): repairs billing code.
- ⚑ **Cair** (@edycutjong): has an FX-rate fallback.
- **Solo License** (@jayaticore): an agent that earns autonomy through verified runs. It is the only entry seen tagging Dodo and Orchestrator.

Coding, devtools and agent-ops entries:
- Patchlane: works through Dependabot PR backlogs
- FirstRun: fixes broken docs. Haimantika retweeted it.
- Upshift
- Kedge
- Mend
- Ouroboros
- Pitstop
- Whittle AI: claims 77% cheaper runs
- Hansa
- Roster
- TeamLoop
- Resurgo
- Interlock
- Crashtest
- TORQUE
- FixLoop
- Heirloom
- DeadEnd
- AutoTrace
- Trueup
- Bingo Whodunit
- release-gate-agent
- Blast Radius
- LeakHound
- Envora
- Friction Fixer
- First User
- Patient Zero

Research, data and other entries:
- VendorLens
- DisruptRadar
- SignalForge
- SignalSDR
- hiring-signal scout
- TruthOps
- DealScout
- Niyam
- TenderOps
- JobReady
- deadmon
- TicketStub

**Sponsors**
- **cfo.ai**: this is Runway Financial (founded 2020), rebranded Sep 10 2026; founder and CEO Siqi Chen ([PR](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cfoai-launches-an-ai-cfo-built-for-founders-302875320.html), [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/09/10/exclusive-ai-finance-cfo-ai-launches-an-agentic-cfo-for-business-founders/)).
  - **It is literally an "AI CFO"**: Ari is billed as an always-on CFO for founders.
  - Ari connects to ledger, payroll, bank, Stripe and CRM data. It outputs a live financial model (assumptions, scenarios, P&L, cash flow, headcount, ARR, runway, board-deck drafts) and sends proactive alerts.
  - It runs on Reambase, a spreadsheet engine built for agents, and you can use it over MCP from a terminal.
  - One outlet (uxc.news) names a different CEO and looks unreliable.
- **Dodo Payments** ([docs](https://docs.dodopayments.com/introduction)): a merchant of record that sells into 220+ countries.
  - Supports one-time, subscription, **usage-based (meters), credit-based** and seat billing.
  - **Full test mode** with test cards, `success@upi`, and webhook simulation through the `dodo` CLI.
  - **Agent Plugin**: an API MCP server, a docs MCP server and 18 skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor ([MCP docs](https://docs.dodopayments.com/developer-resources/mcp-server)).
  - Merchant eligibility depends on the country that issued your ID. **India is eligible. Nigeria has been closed to new merchants since Mar 23 2026**; only existing Nigerian merchants are grandfathered ([list](https://docs.dodopayments.com/miscellaneous/accepted-countries-and-territories)).
  - In this hackathon Dodo is a partner (it supplies the prize credits), not a required tool.
- **Entire** ([entire.io](https://entire.io)): Git hosting for agents. It links each commit to the agent session that produced it (checkpoints), and has an open-source CLI, session sharing and "Trails". The judges come from its DevRel and solutions side.
- **Crustdata** (YC F24): APIs for live company and people data, including headcount, job postings, people search and enrichment, plus Watcher webhooks.
- **Orchestrator.inc** ([site](https://orchestrator.inc/)): a desktop app that runs and supervises fleets of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and 25+ others), each in its own worktree. It routes CI failures and review comments back to the agent that owns the branch. Open source, about 12k stars.
- **TheVibeFounder** (Aj Yadav): co-founder of Otto, 400K+ Instagram followers, emcee. His kickoff theme was distribution.

**Judges**
- **Akshay Hangloo**: pinned post says "Agents are a data problem wearing an AI costume." He wants traces, continuous evals and human feedback stored as data ([post](https://x.com/akshay_hangloo/status/2086745041477968067)). Oct 5: neatlogs keeps agents "working, not just running."
- **Ajay Yadav**: focuses on how to read traces, and on traces as business context. He amplifies cost-from-traces plans.
- **Haimantika Mitra**: retweeted FirstRun, and the point that the session behind a diff is what makes an agent PR trustworthy.
- **Prateek Karnal** (ex-Composio, Databricks, Rippling; 2× ICPC World Finals): "orchestration is the future of all work." He says verification stays human work.
- **Abhi Singh**: Senior Solutions Engineer at Entire, ex-GitHub ([abhisingh.in](https://abhisingh.in/)). No hackathon posts found.

### INFERENCES (not verified)
- The finance and agent-economics space is crowded: Tally, AgentFinOps and Margin all overlap with Syncly's "AI CFO pays agents per job". To stand out, an entry would need real settlement in Dodo test mode, a verified-outcome gate before payout, and cfo.ai unit economics built from neatlogs trace costs. That last pattern is the one Ajay publicly amplified.
- Most entries are developer tools. A non-coding agent that does real business work could score well on originality, but only with hard evidence: before/after numbers and a recovery run.
- The 15% building-in-public score probably rewards several dated posts that tag @neatlogs, @EntireHQ and @arithecfo (cfo.ai's X handle).

The other bits — kickoff workshop notes, the exact Bingo rules, and what judges said on the call — are probably on Discord. I couldn't verify them from the web.

- **Entire** ([entire.io](https://entire.io)): Git hosting for agents. It links each commit to the agent session that produced it (checkpoints), and has an open-source CLI, session sharing and "Trails". The judges come from its DevRel and solutions side.
- **Crustdata** (YC F24): APIs for live company and people data, including headcount, job postings, people search and enrichment, plus Watcher webhooks.
- **Orchestrator.inc** ([site](https://orchestrator.inc/)): a desktop app that runs and supervises fleets of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex and 25+ others), each in its own worktree. It routes CI failures and review comments back to the agent that owns the branch. Open source, about 12k stars.
- **TheVibeFounder** (Aj Yadav): co-founder of Otto, 400K+ Instagram followers, emcee. His kickoff theme was distribution.

### INFERENCES (not verified)
- The finance and agent-economics space is crowded: Tally, AgentFinOps and Margin all overlap with Syncly's "AI CFO pays agents per job". To stand out, an entry would need real settlement in Dodo test mode, a verified-outcome gate before payout, and cfo.ai unit economics built from neatlogs trace costs. That last pattern is the one Ajay publicly amplified.
- Most entries are developer tools. A non-coding agent that does real business work could score well on originality, but only with hard evidence: before/after numbers and a recovery run.
